papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based machine learning model that predicts mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability as a multi-class problem, rather than encoding reference and mutant sequences independently. The authors demonstrate its utility by applying it to the protein CcsZ, showing it can rapidly evaluate large mutational landscapes that would be costly to screen experimentally.

papers.title: Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.
papers.abstract: WHO reports that only 54% of tuberculosis (TB) patients received rapid diagnostic tests at their initial presentation. Conventional laboratory methods in TB detection have high specificity (>90%) but low sensitivity (<50%). This means a large number of tuberculosis patients are missed. A better diagnostic approach is essential to decrease the TB burden. Studies on multi-indicator blood-based models for rapid TB diagnosis remain limited. We developed a rapid, non-sputum-based model to improve the efficiency of TB diagnosis. This was a retrospective case-control study including 301 patients with
papers.summary: This retrospective case-control study developed a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis that combines GBP5 gene expression with routine laboratory indicators. The goal is to improve on conventional TB tests, which have high specificity but low sensitivity and miss many cases. The model aims to provide a rapid, non-sputum-based diagnostic approach.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses reveal VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking environmental bisphenol A exposure to MASH-HCC progression.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC) is an increasingly important subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma, and environmental contaminants have been proposed as potential contributors to its progression. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in metabolic dysfunction and liver injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking BPA exposure to MASH-HCC remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed an integrated framework combining transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis,
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with co-expression network analysis and experimental validation to identify VIPR1 as a potential molecular mediator connecting bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC). The findings suggest that environmental BPA exposure may promote liver cancer progression through VIPR1-related pathways, highlighting a gene-environment interaction in this HCC subtype.

papers.title: Developing SCL2205: A Protein Sequence-based Spatial Modelling Dataset for the Protein Language Model Frontier.
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has substantially advanced protein subcellular localisation (SCL) prediction, yet its potential remains constrained by suboptimal input preparation and limited high-quality reference data. Furthermore, existing state-of-the-art (SoTA) predictors suffer from performance metric inflation due to unmitigated training-to-testing data leakage during homology augmentation. We address these challenges by introducing SCL2205, a leak-minimised benchmark dataset and pipeline curated specifically to support trustworthy, scalable, and reproducible DL-based SCL modelling.
papers.summary: The authors present SCL2205, a new benchmark dataset and pipeline for predicting protein subcellular localization using deep learning. The dataset is specifically designed to minimize data leakage between training and testing sets, addressing a common problem that inflates performance metrics in existing state-of-the-art predictors. This provides a more trustworthy foundation for developing and evaluating protein language models on localization tasks.

papers.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
papers.abstract: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral
papers.summary: VirPLM fine-tunes a protein language model to predict antigenic relationships between influenza A/H3N2 viruses directly from hemagglutinin HA1 sequences, bypassing the need for labor-intensive hemagglutination inhibition assays. This sequence-based approach could enable scalable, high-throughput antigenic surveillance to inform vaccine strain selection.

papers.title: Regulatory-prior-guided attention preserves biological structure during unpaired single-cell RNA-ATAC integration.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing provide complementary views of transcriptional output and chromatin regulatory potential, but integrating unpaired profiles remains challenging because the modalities differ in feature space, sparsity and noise. Existing approaches often frame integration as distribution matching, which can over-align biologically distinct, condition-specific or modality-specific cell states. We present scHPGT, a single-cell Heterogeneous Prior-Guided Transformer for regulatory-prior-guided integration of unpaired RNA and chromatin accessibility profil
papers.summary: The authors introduce scHPGT, a transformer-based method that integrates unpaired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data by incorporating regulatory priors (e.g., gene-peak relationships) rather than relying purely on distribution matching. This prior-guided attention mechanism helps preserve biologically meaningful structure, avoiding over-alignment of distinct cell states that plagues existing integration approaches.

papers.title: Beyond the drug-centric view: Advancing AI virtual cell platforms for environmental perturbation modelling.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality, with their biological effects shaped by factors such as dose, exposure duration, life-stage timing, and cumulative or sequential exposure patterns. With rapid advances in AI based virtual cell (VC) technologies, current frameworks emphasize genet-ic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental perturbations insufficiently modelled. This imbal-ance is due to fundamental structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and representa-tional design, as well as lacking standardized
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI virtual cell platforms are heavily biased toward genetic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental exposures—such as pollutants and chemicals—poorly represented. The authors attribute this gap to structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and model design, and call for standardized frameworks to better model environmental perturbations.

papers.title: Training a force field for proteins and small molecules from scratch.
papers.abstract: Force fields for molecular dynamics are usually developed manually, limiting their transferability and making systematic exploration of functional forms challenging. We developed a graph neural network that assigns all force field parameters for diverse molecules using continuous atom typing. The freely-available model, called Garnet, was trained on quantum mechanical, condensed phase and protein nuclear magnetic resonance data without the use of existing parameters. The resulting force field shows comparable performance to current force fields on small molecules, folded proteins, protein comp
papers.summary: The authors developed Garnet, a graph neural network that assigns force field parameters for both small molecules and proteins using continuous atom typing, trained from scratch on quantum mechanical, condensed-phase, and protein NMR data without relying on existing force field parameters. The resulting force field performs comparably to established force fields on small molecules and folded proteins. This demonstrates that machine-learned force fields can be built systematically rather than through manual parameterization.

papers.title: Gene-specific machine learning model EpiPred identifies likely pathogenic variants in the epilepsy-related gene STXBP1.
papers.abstract: STXBP1 variants are a frequent cause of early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and related neurodevelopmental disorders, but the clinical interpretation of these variants remains a major challenge. Most reported STXBP1 missense variants are classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), complicating diagnosis, counseling, and patient eligibility for precision therapies. Here, we developed EpiPred, a gene-specific machine learning classifier that predicts the pathogenicity of STXBP1 missense variants and tests these predictions using empirical evidence from well-estab
papers.summary: The authors developed EpiPred, a gene-specific machine learning classifier that predicts the pathogenicity of missense variants in STXBP1, a gene frequently implicated in early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. Since most reported STXBP1 missense variants are classified as variants of uncertain significance, EpiPred aims to improve clinical interpretation and patient eligibility for precision therapies. The model's predictions were validated against empirical evidence from well-established functional assays.

papers.title: Shallow recurrent decoders for neural and behavioural dynamics.
papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms are affording new opportunities for building bio-inspired and data-driven models characterizing neural activity. Critical to understanding decision-making and behaviour is quantifying the relationship between the activity of neuronal population codes and individual neurons. We leverage a SHallow REcurrent Decoder (SHRED) architecture for mapping the dynamics of population codes to individual neurons and other proxy measures of neural activity and behaviour. SHRED is constructed from a temporal sequence model, which encodes the temporal dynamics of limited sensor dat
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: This paper applies a shallow recurrent decoder (SHRED) architecture to model how neuronal population codes relate to individual neuron activity and behavioural measures. The approach uses a temporal sequence model to encode dynamics from limited sensor data, offering a lightweight, data-driven method for linking population-level neural dynamics to single-neuron and behavioural outputs.

papers.title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology.
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, human aging has been characterized across DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical modalities, yet no benchmark evaluates whether AI systems can interpret these heterogeneous data types in the context of aging biology. We introduce LongevityBench, an open suite of 17 tasks spanning five biodata domains, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI systems from six developer teams. Despite recent advances in AI, no single model dominates all tasks, with omics-based age prediction being the hardest task regardless of scale. To test whether these gaps can be clos
papers.summary: The authors introduce LongevityBench, an open benchmark of 17 tasks across five biodata domains designed to evaluate how well AI systems can interpret aging-related data. Testing 18 frontier AI models, they find that no single model excels across all tasks, and omics-based age prediction remains the hardest challenge regardless of model scale.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis reveals elevated expression of a transcriptional module implicating specific immune dysregulations in euploid RPL pregnancies, helping to decode the immunological mechanisms behind maternal-fetal tolerance disruption.

papers.title: dicast: a machine learning method for accurate structural variant detection from short-read sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Structural variants are a common cause of human diseases, but their detection from short-read sequencing remains challenging, despite being the technology underlying most clinical workflows. We present dicast, a machine-learning method that scores SV calls from short-read data using alignment and genomic-context features. dicast is trained on a new multi-technology ground truth built from nine samples, with extensive manual curation. It outperforms existing short-read callers and consensus approaches, recovering substantially more true positives at high precision. We also demonstrate dicast's
papers.summary: dicast is a machine-learning method that improves structural variant detection from short-read sequencing by scoring SV calls using alignment and genomic-context features. It was trained on a new multi-technology ground truth dataset from nine samples with extensive manual curation, and outperforms existing short-read callers and consensus approaches, recovering more true positives at high precision.

papers.title: Early Clinical and Cerebrospinal Fluid Predictors of 1-Year Recurrence in Autoimmune GFAP Astrocytopathy.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein astrocytopathy (GFAP-A) is an inflammatory central nervous system disorder with variable outcomes. Relapse occurs in a subset of patients, but early predictors remain unclear. We aimed to identify admission-available features associated with 1-year recurrence and develop an interpretable risk stratification model.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: This study investigates which clinical and cerebrospinal fluid features present at hospital admission can predict whether patients with autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy will experience a relapse within one year. The authors use these early features to build an interpretable risk stratification model, aiming to help clinicians identify high-risk patients for closer monitoring or preventive treatment.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information to predict and interpret protein function, while also supporting natural language interaction. It addresses the gap between models that handle either natural language or genomic code by fusing both modalities, aiming to make DNA-to-function translation more accessible and interpretable.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a computational tool that uses an attention network with bilinear convolution and an adaptive sampling strategy to classify DNA-binding proteins as single-stranded or double-stranded binders. It aims to improve prediction accuracy over existing methods, addressing a gap left by costly experimental approaches. The work is relevant to bioinformatics and drug discovery where identifying DNA-binding protein types is important.

papers.title: Multimodal AI and single-cell transcriptomics integrate to construct a histopathological prognostic model for bladder cancer, revealing the RTN3-glycolysis axis in chemoresistance.
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer is a common malignant tumor of the urinary system, and gemcitabine-based chemotherapy often fails because of drug resistance. Tumor heterogeneity, particularly copy number variations (CNVs) heterogeneity at the genomic level, is a core factor that drives disease progression and drug resistance. However, the relationship between CNV heterogeneity at the single-cell level and the histomorphological features that are relied upon in a routine pathological diagnosis remains unclear, limiting its application in clinical prognostic assessments and precision therapy.
papers.summary: This study integrates multimodal AI with single-cell transcriptomics to build a histopathological prognostic model for bladder cancer, linking genomic copy number variation heterogeneity to tissue morphology. The model identifies an RTN3-glycolysis axis as a driver of gemcitabine chemoresistance, offering a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: ICM-MD: Integrating TM-specific features and MD-derived structures for accurate prediction of inter-chain contacts in α-helical transmembrane homodimers.
papers.abstract: Characterizing the interactions of alpha-helical transmembrane homodimers at the residue level is crucial for understanding their structure and function. However, most computational tools are designed for globular proteins and fail to translate to transmembrane (TM) proteins, largely due to the unique environment of the membrane and the limited availability of high-resolution structural data. To address this challenge, we present a data-centric machine learning framework that overcomes the scarcity of experimentally resolved TM homodimer structures, which are essential for developing a robust
papers.summary: ICM-MD is a machine learning framework that predicts residue-level inter-chain contacts in alpha-helical transmembrane homodimers by combining transmembrane-specific sequence features with molecular dynamics-derived structures. It addresses the scarcity of experimental TM homodimer structures and the poor transferability of globular-protein contact predictors to the membrane environment.

papers.title: Multi-contrast MRI acceleration via post-reconstruction fusion.
papers.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the gold standard for neuroimaging, yet routine brain protocols require multiple high-resolution 3D contrasts (e.g., T1, T2, and T2-FLAIR), resulting in long scan times. Many deep-learning acceleration methods assume access to raw k-space and rely on non-Cartesian trajectories or pseudo-random undersampling patterns, which can require specialized sequence implementations. In this work, we present a practical protocol-level acceleration framework enabled by complementary orthogonal Cartesian acquisitions that can be executed using standard scanner settings. S
papers.summary: This paper introduces a protocol-level MRI acceleration framework that combines multiple orthogonal Cartesian acquisitions (e.g., T1, T2, T2-FLAIR) and fuses them after reconstruction, avoiding the need for raw k-space access or specialized non-Cartesian sequences. The approach enables faster multi-contrast brain imaging using standard scanner settings, making it more practical for clinical deployment.

papers.title: Sequence optimization targeting mRNA stability enhances monoclonal antibody titers in CHO cells.
papers.abstract: This study presents a DNA sequence optimization approach that integrates mRNA stability as a tunable design parameter to enhance monoclonal antibody expression in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. A comprehensive combinatorial library of synonymous coding-sequence variants of an IgG1 light chain was integrated as single copies at a defined genomic locus in CHO cells with identical regulatory elements. Steady-state mRNA abundance, quantified by deep sequencing of gDNA and mRNA, served as a proxy for mRNA stability. These data were used to train a machine learning model that predicts mRNA abund
papers.summary: This study shows that synonymous codon choices affecting mRNA stability can be optimized to boost monoclonal antibody production in CHO cells. By integrating a combinatorial library of light-chain variants at a fixed genomic locus and using deep sequencing to measure mRNA abundance, the authors trained a machine learning model that predicts expression and identifies stabilizing sequences. The optimized sequences increased antibody titers, demonstrating mRNA stability as a tunable design parameter for bioproduction.

papers.title: EmmaEmb: A quantitative framework for analyzing embedding spaces in molecular biology.
papers.abstract: Embeddings, numerical vectors learned by deep-learning models, are increasingly used to represent complex molecular biology data and support predictive tasks and generative design. There is a growing need for systematic approaches to interpret and explain the information encoded in high-dimensional embedding spaces. Here, we introduce EmmaEmb, a quantitative, model-agnostic framework for geometric correction, direct analysis, and comparison of embedding spaces. Our framework encompasses local and global analysis methods to quantify data distribution within an embedding space and enable compari
papers.summary: EmmaEmb is a model-agnostic framework for quantitatively analyzing and comparing embedding spaces in molecular biology, offering geometric correction and both local and global analysis methods. It enables systematic interpretation of what information deep-learning embeddings encode, supporting better comparison across models and datasets.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost editing efficiency while retaining the low off-target profile of the original tBE. This addresses a key limitation of the tBE system, whose modest base editing efficiency has restricted its broader use.

papers.title: Decoding gene regulation in plant genomes with artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: One of the central goals of plant functional genomics is to uncover regulatory mechanisms that shape agriculturally important traits to inform crop improvement. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), especially Large Language Models (LLMs), have greatly transformed our ability to derive regulatory information from complex genomics data. This review starts with a brief introduction of recent advances in AI and ML. We then present a plant-focused synthesis of emerging applications of AI- and LLM tools to: (i) predict epigenomic features, regulatory DNA element
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning and large language models to decode gene regulation in plant genomes, with a focus on predicting epigenomic features and regulatory DNA elements. It highlights how AI tools can extract regulatory information from complex genomics data to inform crop improvement. The paper is aimed at plant functional genomics researchers seeking to leverage AI for understanding agriculturally important traits.

papers.title: Predicting risk of ischemic stroke: A transformer model using genomic data.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide. Genetic factors contribute to IS susceptibility, yet conventional polygenic risk score approaches are primarily based on additive effects and may not fully capture non-linear relationships or positional context and interactions among genetic variants. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a transformer-based genomic model incorporating position-wise genotype embedding for IS risk prediction.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This study develops a transformer-based genomic model that uses position-wise genotype embeddings to predict ischemic stroke risk, aiming to capture non-linear relationships and positional context among genetic variants that conventional additive polygenic risk scores miss. The work represents an application of deep learning architectures to genetic risk prediction in a clinical context.

papers.title: An interpretable framework applying protein words to predict protein-small molecule complementary pairing rules.
papers.abstract: Despite the high accuracy of 'black box' deep learning models, drug discovery still relies on protein-ligand interaction principles and heuristics. To improve interpretability of protein-small molecule binding predictions, we developed the PWRules framework, which applies binding affinity data to identify privileged small molecule fragments and subsequently defines complementary pairing rules between these fragments and protein words (semantic sequence units) through an interpretability module. The resulting word-fragment rules are then used by the PWScore function to prioritize active compoun
papers.summary: The authors present PWRules, an interpretable framework that learns 'protein words' (semantic sequence units) and pairs them with privileged small-molecule fragments using binding affinity data. The derived word-fragment rules feed a PWScore function that ranks active compounds, offering interpretable protein-ligand complementarity rules as an alternative to black-box deep learning models.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Rheumatology and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases: From Pattern Recognition to Signal Analysis and Clinical Decision Support.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are transforming the landscape of rheumatological and systemic inflammatory disease management, offering unprecedented capacity to integrate complex, multidimensional data for diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. This comprehensive narrative review, based on a non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar combined with the authors' clinical expertise, provides a clinically oriented synthesis of current and emerging AI applications across the full spectrum of immune-mediated inflam
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current and emerging applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning in rheumatology and systemic inflammatory diseases, covering diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. It emphasizes the ability of AI/ML to integrate complex, multidimensional clinical data, moving from pattern recognition toward signal analysis and clinical decision support. The review is clinically oriented and based on a non-systematic literature search combined with expert opinion.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models—genomic sequence models and cell foundation models—that learn transferable representations by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens. It argues these models can integrate genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states to tackle complex diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration, and discusses their path toward clinical translation.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification of PIM2 kinase inhibitors through QSAR modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The proto-oncogene serine/threonine kinase PIM2 is a critical regulator of cell proliferation, survival, and tumor progression and represents an attractive therapeutic target for several cancers. In this study, an integrated machine learning-guided computational pipeline was developed to identify potential PIM2 inhibitors by combining quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and pharmacokinetic prediction. Bioactivity data for PIM2 inhibitors were retrieved from the ChEMBL database, yielding 5953 co
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning-based QSAR modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify potential PIM2 kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy. Using bioactivity data from ChEMBL, the authors built predictive models and screened compound libraries to prioritize candidate inhibitors with favorable pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.title: JanusX: an integrated and high-performance platform for scalable genome-wide association studies and genomic selection.
papers.abstract: As genomic datasets expand in both sample size and marker density, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and genomic selection (GS) require workflows that remain statistically rigorous, computationally efficient, and reproducible across the full analysis path, from genotype matrix to decision-relevant outputs. Here we present JanusX, an integrated high-performance framework that provides a streamlined, user-oriented workflow for GWAS and GS by unifying data handling, model execution, and visualization. Across simulated and real datasets, JanusX maintained high concordance with established bas
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: JanusX is an integrated high-performance platform that streamlines genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and genomic selection (GS) by unifying data handling, model execution, and visualization in a single reproducible workflow. It maintains high concordance with established methods across simulated and real datasets while scaling to large sample sizes and marker densities.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive computational paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and emerging approaches—highlighting the strengths and limitations of each. The review is aimed at experienced practitioners and developers seeking a structured overview of phage bioinformatics.

papers.title: HighFold4: extending AlphaFold3 to accurate cyclic peptide conformation prediction via custom chemical connectivity.
papers.abstract: While AlphaFold3 has revolutionized protein structure prediction and supports noncanonical amino acids, its architecture always fails to reliably generate the closed-ring topologies characteristic of cyclic peptides. Existing adaptations, such as imposing distance constraints via an offset matrix, enforce ring geometry but cannot specify the chemical identity of the cyclization bond, leading to a restrictive bias toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles. Here, we present HighFold4, a framework that adapts AlphaFold3 to explicitly incorporate user-defined chemical connectivity between resi
papers.summary: HighFold4 adapts AlphaFold3 to accurately predict cyclic peptide conformations by explicitly encoding user-defined chemical connectivity for ring-closing bonds, overcoming AlphaFold3's inability to reliably generate closed-ring topologies. Unlike prior approaches that use distance constraints and bias predictions toward amide- or disulfide-linked macrocycles, this framework supports diverse cyclization chemistries. This extends AlphaFold3's utility to a broader class of therapeutically relevant macrocyclic peptides.

papers.title: FatPlants 2.0: an AI-powered platform integrating plant lipid genes, pathways, and literature.
papers.abstract: Plant lipid research depends on accessible databases that connect genes, pathways, and prior literature. However, currently available resources are fragmented, species-limited, and lack AI-powered interfaces for integrated querying. FatPlants 2.0 addresses these issues by integrating ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental data into a unified platform with 14 000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways across 5 species, and 57 000+ curated publications. The platform features LipidBot, an AI agent enabling natural language queries via graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented ge
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: FatPlants 2.0 is an updated database platform that unifies plant lipid gene, pathway, and literature data from ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental datasets, covering 14,000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways, and 57,000+ publications across five species. It introduces LipidBot, an AI agent that lets researchers query this integrated resource using natural language, combining graph-based pathway search with retrieval-augmented generation.

papers.title: PhoSARte: identification of SARS-CoV-2 phosphorylation sites using contrastive learning and protein language models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation, a critical post-translational modification, is extensively altered during viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, where it plays a central role in modulating host-pathogen interactions. Accurately identifying these specific phosphorylation sites is crucial for understanding viral pathogenesis, prioritizing antiviral targets, guiding therapeutic strategies, and strengthening preparedness for future viral outbreaks. Although several computational tools have been proposed to complement experimental phosphoproteomics, existing methods often show limited robustness, cross-viral gen
papers.summary: PhoSARte is a computational tool that uses contrastive learning combined with protein language models to predict phosphorylation sites specifically in SARS-CoV-2 proteins. It aims to improve on existing phosphoproteomics prediction methods, which often lack robustness and cross-viral generalization. The tool is intended to help identify host-pathogen interaction points relevant to antiviral target prioritization.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The authors present a structure-based dual-driven graph transformer framework that incorporates a pretrained protein language model to classify bacterial virulence factors into functional classes. By combining sequence-derived language model embeddings with spatial structure information, the method improves prediction of virulence factor categories compared to sequence-only approaches. This supports understanding of bacterial pathogenesis and identification of potential antivirulence targets.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: KGTC-DDA is a computational framework that predicts drug-disease associations by combining parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks linked via cross-attention. This hybrid architecture aims to capture both local structural patterns in the drug-disease knowledge graph and global dependencies, improving drug repurposing predictions over prior graph neural network methods.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a RoBERTa-based framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to predict molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This transformer approach aims to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery, which is a rapidly growing therapeutic area with 24 FDA-approved RNA drugs and over 130 in clinical trials.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins by combining chemical and protein large language models for feature representation with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach aims to expand the computational toolkit for metabolite-protein interaction prediction, which is relevant to systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent): an interpretable hybrid generative Artificial Intelligence agent for expression-grounded discovery in single-cell genomics.
papers.abstract: Translating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data into mechanistic biological hypotheses remains a critical bottleneck, as agentic AI systems lack direct access to transcriptomic representations while expression foundation models remain opaque to natural language. Here, we introduce ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent), an interpretable framework that unifies single-cell generative pretrained transformer expression embeddings with biomedical bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based semantic retrieval and large-language model (LLM)-mediated interpret
papers.summary: ELISA is a hybrid AI agent that combines single-cell expression foundation model embeddings with biomedical text retrieval and LLM reasoning to help researchers generate mechanistic hypotheses from scRNA-seq data. It bridges the gap between opaque expression models and natural-language interpretation, enabling expression-grounded, interpretable discovery in single-cell genomics.

papers.title: From pixels to conservation: Deep learning for automated monitoring of rare and endangered wildlife.
papers.abstract: Conservation of rare and endangered species requires scalable monitoring solutions to address accelerating biodiversity loss. Deep learning has transformed wildlife monitoring, enabling automated species identification, individual tracking, demographic inference, and behavioral analysis from camera traps, drones, and video surveillance. This review systematically analyzes 159 wildlife monitoring studies (2014-2026) across four technical domains: species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis. We examine architectural evolutio
papers.summary: This review systematically analyzes 159 deep learning studies from 2014-2026 on automated wildlife monitoring, covering species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis from camera traps, drones, and video. It synthesizes architectural evolution and methodological trends to support scalable conservation monitoring of rare and endangered species.

papers.title: Predicting non-specific binding of VHHs using machine learning models with cluster-aware validation.
papers.abstract: Propensity for nonspecific binding-also known as polyreactivity-is a serious developability risk factor for biotherapeutic candidates. To minimize this risk, drug companies are increasingly relying on in silico tools utilizing machine learning methods, but developing these tools is challenging. For example, the available data often contains many closely related sequences originating from drug pipeline projects, which can introduce significant biases in the in silico models training and benchmarking, leading to poor generalizability on new data. We present here a workflow designed to diagnose a
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning workflow for predicting nonspecific binding (polyreactivity) of VHH antibody fragments, a key developability risk for biotherapeutics. The authors emphasize that standard random train/test splits are misleading because datasets contain many closely related sequences from drug pipelines, so they introduce cluster-aware validation to avoid over-optimistic performance estimates and improve generalizability to new sequences.

papers.title: PMAVP: A Mamba-Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Antiviral Peptide Identification and Functional Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate computational prediction of antiviral peptides (AVPs) can accelerate peptide screening and reduce experimental costs. However, existing deep learning-based methods still suffer from severe class imbalance, over-reliance on handcrafted features and limited interpretability. Here, we propose PMAVP, a multi-task learning framework that integrates the ProtT5 pre-trained protein language model with a Mamba-inspired module for AVP identification and functional activity prediction. We use ProtT5 to extract deep semantic representations from peptide sequences and a Mamba module to capture lon
papers.summary: PMAVP is a multi-task deep learning framework that combines the ProtT5 protein language model with a Mamba-inspired sequence module to identify antiviral peptides and predict their functional activity. It aims to overcome class imbalance, reliance on handcrafted features, and limited interpretability in prior methods. The approach offers a computational tool to accelerate antiviral peptide screening and reduce experimental costs.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review surveys deep learning approaches for decoding plant cis-regulatory information, comparing convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph neural network architectures. It evaluates how these models integrate DNA sequence with multi-omics data to predict transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and prioritize non-coding variants. The paper highlights both the promise and current limitations of applying these methods to plant genomes.

papers.title: scGPA: an LLM-assisted workflow for directional virtual gene perturbation analysis from single-cell transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Existing virtual perturbation methods can often infer directional changes by comparing predicted post-perturbation expression profiles with control cells. However, workflows that directly return direction-specific downstream candidate genes together with confidence scores, evidence support and interpretable summaries remain limited. We developed scGPA, an LLM-assisted workflow system for directional single-cell virtual gene perturbation analysis.
papers.summary: scGPA is an LLM-assisted workflow for virtual gene perturbation analysis in single-cell transcriptomes, designed to return direction-specific downstream candidate genes along with confidence scores, evidence support, and interpretable summaries. It addresses the gap left by existing methods that can infer directional changes but rarely provide integrated, interpretable outputs for downstream gene candidates.

papers.title: Cross-Virus RNA Language Models for Within-Family RNA-RNA Interaction Prediction in SARS-CoV-2 and Porcine Deltacoronavirus.
papers.abstract: RNA large language models (RNA LLMs) show potential for predicting viral RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs), but their ability to transfer between viruses remains unclear. Here, we evaluated three nucleotide language models using vRIC-seq-derived RRI datasets from two members of the Coronaviridae family, SARS-CoV-2 and porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV). We compared within-virus five-fold cross-validation with bidirectional cross-virus testing. DNABERT achieved within-virus AUC values of 0.9595 for PDCoV and 0.9741 for SARS-CoV-2. Under cross-virus transfer, its AUC decreased to 0.8372 when trained on
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether RNA language models trained to predict RNA-RNA interactions in one coronavirus can transfer to another. DNABERT performed strongly within each virus (AUC ~0.96-0.97) but dropped to ~0.84 when transferred across viruses, showing that cross-virus generalization remains a challenge. The work highlights both the promise and current limits of RNA LLMs for viral interaction prediction.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Lower Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis in Patients with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) have an increased risk of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) due to inflammation, immobility, and coagulation abnormalities. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for predicting DVT risk in AECOPD patients and identify important predictors.
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning model to predict lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk in patients hospitalized with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), a population at elevated thrombotic risk. The model identifies key clinical predictors, offering a potential tool for early risk stratification in this specific patient group.

papers.title: Artificial-intelligence- and multi-omics-guided predictive and drug repurposing framework construction for colorectal cancer: evidence from succinylation-neutrophil signatures.
papers.abstract: Succinylation-linked metabolic rewiring and neutrophil-driven inflammation are key drivers of colorectal carcinoma (COAD) progression; however, they have rarely been translated to an end-to-end artificial intelligence (AI) drug-design pipeline connecting target nomination, resistance-relevant tumor microenvironment states, and candidate evaluation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study builds an AI- and multi-omics-driven framework for colorectal cancer that links succinylation-related metabolic rewiring and neutrophil-driven inflammation to candidate drug targets. The authors use these 'succinylation-neutrophil' signatures to nominate targets and repurpose existing drugs, aiming to connect tumor microenvironment states with therapeutic evaluation. It represents an integrative computational pipeline rather than a wet-lab validated discovery.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis identifies CCL22-associated immune signatures in air pollution-related atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Air pollution has been associated with the development and exacerbation of atopic dermatitis (AD), but the molecular signatures connecting pollutant-related targets with AD-associated immune dysregulation remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data to identify molecular links between air pollution exposure and atopic dermatitis, highlighting CCL22-associated immune signatures. The findings suggest that pollutant-related gene expression changes may drive immune dysregulation in AD, offering potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Deciphering the therapeutic mechanisms of Qingfei Litan prescription in acute lung injury: an integrated framework of UHPLC-MS/MS, systems pharmacology, machine learning, and in vivo validation.
papers.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is primarily defined by hyper-inflammation and the breakdown of the alveolar-capillary barrier, frequently culminating in refractory respiratory failure. Current clinical interventions-predominantly glucocorticoids and supportive therapies-often yield suboptimal outcomes and are associated with significant side effects. Qingfei Litan Prescription (QFLTP), a traditional Chinese medical prescription indicated for inflammatory respiratory disorders, exhibits significant therapeutic potential; however, the precise molecular mechanisms driving its protective effects are curr
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates UHPLC-MS/MS chemical profiling, systems pharmacology, machine learning, and in vivo validation to uncover how Qingfei Litan Prescription (QFLTP) protects against acute lung injury. The authors identify the prescription's active compounds and their likely molecular targets and pathways, then confirm the anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects in animal models. The work provides a mechanistic rationale for a traditional Chinese medicine formula in treating ALI.

papers.title: Predictive model for ulcerative colitis therapeutic response using clinical indicators and peripheral blood T-cell subsets.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to integrate clinical indicators with peripheral blood T-cell subsets to develop a prediction model for ulcerative colitis (UC), and to facilitate precise subtyping and individualized treatment decisions.
papers.summary: This study builds a predictive model for how ulcerative colitis patients will respond to therapy by combining routine clinical indicators with measurements of T-cell subsets in peripheral blood. The goal is to enable more precise patient subtyping and individualized treatment decisions.

papers.title: Identification of Wnt/β-catenin- and immune-related genes in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury using bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and a murine model.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is a major complication following liver transplantation (LT), contributing to graft dysfunction and rejection. The roles of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and immune responses in LT-related HIRI remain incompletely elucidated. This study aimed to screen key genes associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling scores and immune regulation in HIRI after LT.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and a murine model to identify genes linked to Wnt/β-catenin signaling and immune regulation in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury following liver transplantation. The authors screen for key genes associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling scores and immune responses, aiming to clarify their roles in graft dysfunction and rejection.

papers.title: Potential hazard assessment of 6PPD-quinone in the context of ulcerative colitis: network toxicology, machine learning, transcriptomic analysis, and preliminary In vivo validation.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) poses potential systemic health risks, yet its toxicological impact on the intestinal tract, particularly in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC), remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether 6PPD-Q aggravates DSS-induced colitis and to identify candidate molecular events using integrative computational and experimental approaches.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone worsens ulcerative colitis, using network toxicology, machine learning, and transcriptomic analysis combined with preliminary in vivo validation in a DSS-induced colitis model. The authors identify candidate molecular events linking 6PPD-Q exposure to colitis aggravation, suggesting a potential environmental risk factor for intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Decoding the Bone-Eye Axis: Machine Learning for Age-Related Macular Degeneration Risk Prediction.
papers.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, yet systemic determinants of its risk remain incompletely understood. Bone mineral density (BMD), a marker of skeletal and biological aging, may reflect shared pathways linking systemic and retinal degeneration. We investigated the association between BMD and AMD using a multilayered framework integrating epidemiological analyses, Mendelian randomization (MR), proteomic and metabolomic profiling, machine learning, and an experimental low-BMD model. Across 3 cohorts, including UK Biobank, National Health and
papers.summary: This study investigates whether bone mineral density (BMD) is linked to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using a multi-layered approach combining epidemiology, Mendelian randomization, proteomics, metabolomics, machine learning, and a low-BMD animal model. The findings suggest that BMD, as a marker of biological aging, may share systemic pathways with retinal degeneration and could help predict AMD risk.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. Here, we present a simple generative approach for creating synthetic 5'-UTR libraries based solely on the genomic sequence statistics of any desired organism. T
papers.summary: The authors present a generative language model that creates synthetic 5'-UTR sequence libraries using only the genomic sequence statistics of a target organism, without requiring prior mechanistic knowledge or validated genetic parts. This approach aims to enable translational tuning in non-model organisms where predictive design tools are scarce.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a conditional protein language model that produces sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers, by testing their stability in molecular dynamics simulations. The generated sequences exhibit high structural stability, suggesting that protein language models can produce biologically plausible enzymes with favorable biophysical properties.

papers.title: Multimodal molecular features enable interpretable umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are important taste-active components in protein-rich foods, but their computational discovery is still constrained by predictors that rely mainly on sequence information and provide limited mechanistic interpretability. In this study, BioPP-GFD was developed as an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework for umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis. The model integrates molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors through adaptive channel attention. In the umami-bitter peptide classification task, BioPP-GFD achieved an accurac
papers.summary: BioPP-GFD is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors to screen for umami peptides with improved interpretability. It outperforms sequence-only predictors in distinguishing umami from bitter peptides and provides mechanistic insights into structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: BeitAI-pHLA: Multiallele Peptide-HLA Class I Binding Prediction Using Protein Language Model and Multi-Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules participate in cellular immune responses by binding to peptide fragments derived from antigens. Exploring this process is crucial to understanding the mechanisms and underlying factors that regulate the cellular immune system. Due to the extreme polymorphism of HLA, the peptides obtained from mass spectrometry of eluted ligand experiments typically correspond to multiple HLA alleles. They are thus poly-specific, providing various options for HLA assignments. This introduces notable challenges for accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation. To add
papers.summary: BeitAI-pHLA is a new computational method for predicting which peptides bind to class I HLA molecules, a key step in immune recognition. It uses a protein language model combined with multi-instance learning to handle the challenge that mass-spectrometry eluted ligands often come from multiple HLA alleles at once, making binding assignment ambiguous. This approach aims to improve accuracy in multi-allele peptide-HLA binding prediction.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking.
papers.abstract: Background: Virtual screening outcomes depend on protocol choices normally made implicitly by experts. I tested whether encoding that expertise as a "skill file" (a Markdown reference read by a large-language-model coding agent) changes virtual screening outcomes versus naive agent defaults, in a single-target case study on formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2; Protein Data Bank 7T6S, 3.0 Å cryo-electron microscopy). Methods: A Claude Code agent curated 1,000 pChEMBL ≥5 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries under naive and skill-guided protocols, and screened the
papers.summary: This case study tests whether encoding expert virtual-screening protocol choices into a Markdown 'skill file' that guides a large-language-model coding agent improves screening outcomes for the formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) target. The agent curated 1,000 known FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys and compared naive versus skill-guided ligand preparation and docking workflows. It demonstrates a practical framework for LLM-coordinated, physics- and diffusion-based docking in a single-target setting.

papers.title: Integrating domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers for transparent cervical cancer diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer screening relies heavily on manual cytopathological evaluation, which is subjective and prone to inter-observer variability. While deep learning offers automated alternatives, existing models often struggle to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological nuances. To address this, we propose CAMF-Swin, a novel hybrid architecture for precise cervical cell classification.
papers.summary: The authors propose CAMF-Swin, a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers to classify cervical cells for cancer screening. The goal is to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological detail, addressing the subjectivity and inter-observer variability of manual cytopathology. The abstract presents the method as a novel approach but does not report quantitative results.
